about.intro_content: Prof. Jian-Chuan Xia is Professor and Director of the Department of Cell Therapy and Healthcare Research Center at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou. He completed postdoctoral training in tumour immunotherapy and tumorigenesis at the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Harvard Medical School.
about.detailed_content: Prof. Xia's research spans two main areas: cancer genetics, investigating tumour suppressor genes such as ING2, TESTIN, BATF2, LZAP and BIN1 in hepatocellular carcinoma and gastric cancer; and cancer immunotherapy, developing cell-based treatments including cytokine-induced killer (CIK) cells, natural killer (NK) cells, dendritic cells (DC), and DC-CIK combination therapy. He has also investigated dendritic cell/tumour fusion vaccines and genetically modified DC vaccines for cancer treatment, and has published more than 80 research papers.

faq.section_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Prof. Jian-Chuan Xia

items.question: Does Prof. Jian-Chuan Xia accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to cell-based cancer immunotherapy at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What is Prof. Xia's area of specialisation?
items.answer: Prof. Xia specialises in cell-based cancer immunotherapy, including CIK cell, dendritic cell and NK cell treatment, alongside cancer genetics research.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: What is cell-based immunotherapy and who might it help?
items.answer: Cell-based immunotherapy uses a patient's own immune cells, such as CIK or dendritic cells, to target cancer; Prof. Xia's research suggests it may help reduce recurrence when combined with other treatments such as ablation, though suitability depends on individual case assessment.

items.question: Does Prof. Xia conduct research beyond immunotherapy?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Xia also researches tumour suppressor genes in hepatocellular carcinoma and gastric cancer, examining their role in tumour progression and prognosis.
